title: Domatokeftedes
subtitle: Greek tomato fritters from Santorini
excerpt: Ripe tomatoes, mint, and onion bound with flour and fried until crisp. A Santorini classic that works as a starter or a side dish alongside grilled fish.
sourceNotes: Drawn from the Santorini tradition of tomato fritters using the island's small, sweet tomatoes. Adapted for standard supermarket tomatoes.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Mix the batter up to 2 hours ahead and keep chilled. Fry just before serving.

content.text: Domatokeftedes are fried tomato patties packed with fresh mint and onion. The batter should be loose enough to drop from a spoon but thick enough to hold shape. Squeeze out as much liquid as possible from the tomatoes or the fritters will spread and splatter.

items.prepNote: roughly grated, excess juice squeezed out

content.text: Grate the tomatoes on the coarse side of the box grater into a bowl. Discard the skins. Squeeze the grated flesh in your hands over the sink and remove as much liquid as you can.
Grate the onion on the fine side of the grater. Add it to the tomato along with the mint, parsley, salt, and pepper.
Stir in the flour a little at a time until the mixture holds together when pressed. It should be thick but not stiff.
Cover the bowl and chill for 30 minutes. This helps the mixture firm up.
Heat the olive oil in the frying pan over a medium heat. Drop heaped tablespoons of the mixture into the pan and press lightly to form patties.
Fry for 3 to 4 minutes per side until deep golden and firm. Work in batches to avoid crowding.
Lift out with a slotted spoon and drain on a plate lined with kitchen paper. Serve hot.

items.symptom: The fritters spread and break apart.
items.cause: Too much liquid remained in the tomatoes, or the mixture was too loose.
items.fix: Squeeze the tomato flesh again and stir in a little more flour until the mixture holds its shape when pressed.

items.symptom: The outside colours before the centre sets.
items.fix: Lower the heat to medium-low and give each side a full 4 minutes. The centre needs time to cook through.

items.cause: The tomatoes were watery and low in flavour, or the seasoning was too light.
items.fix: Taste the raw mixture before chilling and adjust salt. A pinch more dried oregano also lifts the flavour.
